executiveSummary: **Recommend C: retain a single call with Qwen3 4B for local development, improve the prompt/schema guidance and grounding/safety checks before approving production use.** Qwen3 is the stronger classifier/extractor and fits fully on this GPU. Qwen2.5 has a slightly higher subjective draft mean (2.54 versus 2.23), but misses complaint priority, fails the quote contract often and needs CPU offload. Neither unchanged baseline produces reliable staff-ready prose. Two-call Qwen3 gives better prose on its completed drafts, but loses two extraction cases and adds substantial latency/token use; splitting is not yet justified as the default architecture.
architectureFindings: On the same subset, current single-call Qwen3 averages 2.03/5 over 36 drafts, two-call 4.30/5 over 10 generated drafts (2/12 extraction failures), and improved single-call 3.08/5 over all 12. Two-call median is 7.76 s versus 3.09 s for improved single-call and 2.65 s for the current single-call subset. Measured input/output tokens per enquiry are 606.5/381.7 for two-call, 506.8/172.8 for improved single-call, and 371.8/155.8 for current single-call: approximately 45% more total tokens than improved single-call, and 87% more than current single-call. Two-call produced no unsafe drafts among its ten completed Qwen3 drafts, but its schema/grounding failures remain material; improved single-call retained 12/12 valid classifications and 68/78 correct fields versus 10/12 and 63/78 for two-call. The tested single-call amendment is still imperfect: role-instruction text leaks into drafts, event replies sometimes include a room token, and one draft invents corrections. It is evidence that targeted instruction changes help, not a production-ready replacement. The tested two-call Qwen2.5 path still misclassified the injection as wedding and produced unsafe inventory assertions. These small experimental samples justify further review, not claims of statistical superiority or a cross-model combination that was never tested.
finalRecommendation: **C — improve the single-call prompt/schema, using qwen3:4b-instruct locally.** Preserve one structured classification/extraction/draft call and independent server routing, trusted pricing, safe-template fallback and human review. Prioritize explicit resort voice, correct standalone/category-specific quote usage, missing versus zero semantics, contradiction/invalid-input handling, budget-versus-price distinctions and factual consistency before quoting. Strengthen guards for unsupported availability/confirmation claims and multilingual/perspective gaps. The current implementation and the experimental amended prompt both need review before production approval. Do not select B: 7B missed nine of twelve complaint-priority checks in the primary sample and gains no demonstrated overall advantage on this hardware. Do not adopt D yet: the measured Qwen3 split improves prose but is about 2.5 times as slow as the improved single-call condition, consumes about 45% more tokens per enquiry, and fails extraction twice. If future staff-editing measurements justify a split, the measured promising candidate is Qwen3 at both stages, followed by a larger controlled extraction/safety evaluation; no mixed-model pipeline was measured. The approved local 30-minute timeout remains a development accommodation; hosted providers retain ten-second attempts. A suitable hosted Haiku API should remove dependence on this laptop's GPU/offload, but hosted latency, rate limits, quality, schema compatibility and timeout sufficiency have not been verified.
